en: The solid ice in a traditional halo-halo melts into a liquid when exposed to the hot tropical sun.
The iron body of a colorful jeepney undergoes a chemical change called oxidation when it rusts in the rainy season.
Squeezing fresh calamansi and dissolving brown sugar in water creates a homogeneous mixture known as a solution.
Translucent capiz shells, harvested from marine snails in Capiz province, allow light to pass through diffusely for window panels.
Fermenting coconut sap into tuba involves a chemical change where natural yeasts convert the liquid sugars into alcohol.
Taal Volcano in Batangas releases water vapor, which is matter in a gaseous state, during its volcanic eruptions.
A bowl of binignit is a heterogeneous mixture because you can easily see and separate its solid ingredients like sago.
Abaca plants, native to the Philippines, produce strong natural fibers that are highly resistant to saltwater damage for making ropes.
Fishermen in General Santos City freeze their freshly caught yellowfin tuna in solid ice blocks to preserve the meat.
Burning dried coconut leaves, called dahon ng niyog, produces heat and ash through an irreversible chemical change called combustion.
Extracting gata from grated mature coconuts creates a mixture that eventually separates into distinct layers of water and coconut oil.
Boiling water in a traditional palayok clay pot causes a physical change as the liquid water turns into invisible water vapor.
